evidence: AES-256-CBC/PKCS7 wrapper decrypts an embedded PowerShell script and invokes the resulting ScriptBlock.

The decoded script reverses Base64/XOR/Base64 into a 64,000-byte managed injector, reflectively loads FILE.WHORE and invokes LAUNCHER with a .NET Framework aspnet_compiler host path and a separate 286,208-byte native PE.

Resolved CIL traces LAUNCHER through a delegate array: process creation uses 0x08000004 (hidden+suspended), reads the supplied PE headers and entry RVA, obtains a 179-int x86 context with flags 0x10002, reads/replaces the remote image, allocates 0x3000/0x40 memory, writes headers/sections and the PEB image base, places mapped-base+entry RVA into CONTEXT[44] (Eax), sets context and resumes the thread.
The PowerShell loop checks local process presence and retries when the host disappears. Despite its Beacon Controller comment, this loop itself has no network beacon.
Layered concealment and suspended-host image transplantation establish malicious loader behavior without relying on VT, family attribution, or runtime success.
samples.marker_line: Secure loader: AES/XOR stages hollow host; added liveness coverage

evidence: Incomplete Android Accessibility/ADB provisioning demonstrator, with example package identifiers and a reserved .invalid endpoint. No package manifest, invocation entry point, deployment record or supplied native helper accompanies it.

enrollAndRun opens developer settings, clicks available Accessibility nodes, accepts a pairing code from its caller, requests a secure-settings grant, launches a local lib-prefixed helper, reinstalls an APK with installer attribution/runtime grants, enables Accessibility, exempts the app from Doze and starts getevent.

The TaskListener class has no callback implementation. No received task is bound to an ADB command. recoverCredential only calls an arithmetic coordinate-to-keypad helper, is never called by the enrollment code, and receives no getevent data. The credential category and X/Y strings are unused constants.

There is no shown credential storage, theft or exfiltration, no auto-extraction of a pairing code, and no restoration-after-uninstall path. The class also omits required abstract AccessibilityService callbacks, consistent with a snippet rather than a deployable application.

The fixed administrative provisioning and raw-input command remain dual-use capabilities. Disconnected theft/control markers and missing implementation tip the supplied artifact to BENIGN; accompanying native code or actual deployment could change that assessment.
samples.classifier_assessment: No calibrated flag after correction; consistent with BENIGN despite residual raw probability

evidence: Creates a visually spoofed C:\Windows \System32 stage, requests a Defender exclusion for it and writes its executable path into the HKCU Run key.

Polls Telegram getUpdates every 20 seconds; reads document file IDs from received updates; resolves getFile metadata; downloads the returned Telegram file path into the executable destination and starts that same destination with a hidden window.
The repeated document-to-process handoff is an operator task channel. Concealed launch, Defender exclusion, deceptive system location and logon reactivation tip the verdict to MALICIOUS.

BOT_TOKEN, operator documents, permissions and Windows path handling determine runtime success. The script does not track the Telegram update offset, so existing documents may be executed again. No document contents or final executable are supplied.
